findings.F1: The supporting check failed because the forecast hit its cap, not because the effect is ungraded: 69 % of the 160 cases in folds B and C (median forecast -20, mean -18.8) sit at the -20 cap, so no cases are above the median size and step 5's check returned None. Meanwhile the main measure is on the predicted side: an unusual short move of +2.26 % per case, t 2.47, on 79 days, strength 0.40.
findings.F2: Inside the tested situation, which already requires a fall of at least one usual 5-day move, the next-day fall does not grow with depth. By prior 5-day fall tercile it is +3.25 % (shallow, t 2.80), +0.80 % (mid, t 0.62) and +2.66 % (deep, t 1.65). By forecast tercile it is +2.84 %, +1.80 % and +2.15 %. The threshold has removed the gradient the idea claims.
findings.F3: Across all wide up days in a falling market, whatever the prior week (390 cases, 160 days, +1.01 %, t 2.24), the next-day fall grows with the depth of the previous 5-day move, measured in usual 5-day moves:
findings.F4: On the same 390 wide up days in falling markets, the next-day fall also grows with the day's width against its 20-day mean range: +0.41 % (t 0.63), +0.88 % (t 1.39) and +1.75 % (t 2.45, strength 0.31) from the least wide to the widest tercile.
findings.F5: The fade is broad, not carried by one coin or one period. It is positive on 10 of 12 coins, with ETH at +3.21 % (t 3.99), BTC +2.79 % (t 2.46), LTC +2.36 % (t 2.52) and ZEC +2.12 % (t 2.33). It is also positive in 8 of 10 windows. The test already used every coin and fold available, so there is no more data to add.

ideas.idea: In a falling market, a wide up day is followed by a fall over the next day, and the deeper the coin's fall over its previous 5 days, the larger the next day's fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should sell for one day into every wide bounce in a downtrend, betting more the harder the coin fell over the week before it, and least when the week was flat or up.
ideas.name: falling wide bounce depth-graded

ideas.idea: In a falling market, an up day whose high-low range is wide against the coin's mean daily range of the last 20 days is followed by a fall over the next day, and the wider the day, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should fade the widest up days of a downtrend for one day, sized by how wide the day was against the coin's recent ranges.
ideas.name: falling wide up-day width fade
